library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

```{r model-meta, include = FALSE}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Rieger_2022_liver_lipid_qsp"))
```

* Citation: `r mod$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2022.910789> (open access, PMC9343875)
* Source code: <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6621096> (Julia, v1.1). The
  article describes the model in prose and Figure 1 only; the ODEs are in
  `dxdt.jl`, the parameter values in `parameters_pluto.csv`, their derivation in
  `derived_parameters.jl`, the liver-fat observable in `util.jl` and the
  intervention settings in `main.jl`. Supplementary Table S1 prints the same
  basal values to two significant figures.

Rieger 2022 is a quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) model of human
hepatocyte lipid metabolism, built to simulate anti-steatotic therapies in
non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). Five ODEs track cytosolic fatty
acids (`fa_cy`), cytosolic triglyceride (`tg_cy`), endoplasmic-reticulum fatty
acids and triglyceride (`fa_er`, `tg_er`), and lumped plasma triglyceride
(`tg_p`). The fluxes are 24-hour averages, so time is in days and the model has
no meal dynamics. Pioglitazone and diet are not given as doses: each is a step
change in one or more of the `scale_*` flux multipliers.

Nothing in the model is estimated. The authors derived a basal parameter set
from literature fluxes and steady-state constraints, then built virtual patients
by sampling the first 14 parameters and keeping those whose steady state
matches the joint distribution of liver fat and plasma triglyceride in Kotronen
2007. The packaged model therefore carries no IIV and no residual error. This
vignette rebuilds a virtual population the same way and uses it to reproduce
Figures 2 to 5.

# Population

```{r population, echo = FALSE}
pop <- mod$population
tibble::tibble(Field = names(pop), Value = vapply(pop, paste, character(1), collapse = " ")) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

# Source trace

| Model element | Source |
|---|---|
| ODEs `d/dt(fa_cy)` to `d/dt(tg_p)` | `dxdt.jl` (`dfa_cy`, `dtg_cy`, `dfa_er`, `dtg_er`, `dtg_p`); Figure 1 schematic |
| Flux expressions (`nefa_uptake`, `er_uptake`, `tg_cy_ester`, `tg_cy_lipo`, `tg_er_ester`, `tg_er_vldl_prod`, `tg_p_liver_uptake`, `tg_p_clear`, `chylo_prod`, `dnl`, `beta_ox`) | `dxdt.jl` "Fluxes" block |
| ER lipolysis set to zero | `dxdt.jl` (`tg_er_lipo = 0.0`, with its footnote on ATGL) |
| Cytosolic-FA feedback on NEFA uptake, smooth max with k = 20 and floor `fa_cy_basal / 10` | `dxdt.jl` (`h(k, x, minx)`, `denom`, `nefa_uptake_feedback`); Section 2.2 |
| DNL feedback on beta-oxidation | `dxdt.jl` (`beta_ox_feedback`); Section 2.2 |
| Initial conditions = basal concentrations | `main.jl` (`x0 .= df.TV[23:27]`) |
| `liver_fat` (volume %), TG density 0.9 g/mL, MW 772 g/mol, non-TG hepatocyte volume 0.95 x 0.7089 L | `util.jl` `getLTGprct` (vector method); `derived_parameters.jl` |
| All 27 `ini()` values | `parameters_pluto.csv` TV column (rows 1-27); Table S1 for rows 1-14 |
| Pioglitazone: `scale_nefa_uptake` 0.725 for 24 weeks | `main.jl` (`nefa_scalar = 1 - 0.275`, `tspan = 24 * 7`); Section 2.5 (-28%) |
| Diet: `scale_chylo` 0.8, `scale_dnl` 0.448, `scale_nefa_uptake` 0.89 for 26 weeks | `main.jl`; Section 2.6 (-20%, -55%, -11%) |
| Sensitivity analysis: `scale_dnl`, `scale_nefa_uptake`, `scale_tg_ester` from 1 to 0.05; `scale_vldl_prod` from 1 to 20 | `main.jl` (`sa_scale`, `p_idx_scale`, `p_scale_inv`); Section 2.7 |
| Plausible-patient prior (log-normal, mean TV, SD (HV - LV) / 3.24, parameters 1-14) and steady-state bounds (rows 23-27) | `mh.jl`, `mh_sim.jl`, `parameters_pluto.csv` LV / HV columns |
| Target distribution of liver fat and plasma TG | `util.jl` `joint_tg_dist` (176 digitised Kotronen 2007 points, TG / 0.8) |
| Virtual-patient selection | `select_vps.jl` (5-nearest-neighbour density, acceptance-rejection) |
| Published simulated means (Figures 3, 4, 5) | Digitised by the maintainers from the article figures |

# Steady state of the basal parameter set

The basal values were derived so that every pool is at steady state. Solving
the typical patient for 1000 days confirms it: no state moves by more than
about 1 part in 100,000. The NEFA-uptake feedback is not exactly 1 at basal
because its smooth-max denominator is 0.1494 mM rather than 0.15 mM, which
accounts for the tiny drift.

```{r steady-state}
ss_typ <- rxSolve(mod, et(c(0, 1000)), returnType = "data.frame")
ss_typ |>
  select(time, fa_cy, tg_cy, fa_er, tg_er, tg_p, liver_fat) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 5)

drift <- abs(unlist(ss_typ[2, c("fa_cy", "tg_cy", "fa_er", "tg_er", "tg_p")]) /
  unlist(ss_typ[1, c("fa_cy", "tg_cy", "fa_er", "tg_er", "tg_p")]) - 1)
stopifnot(max(drift) < 1e-4)
```

The typical patient has `r round(ss_typ$liver_fat[1], 2)`% liver fat, so it is
just below the 5% NAFLD threshold. Its 24-hour mean plasma triglyceride is
1.54 mM (136 mg/dL).

## Fatty-acid mass balance

At steady state the hepatocyte's fatty-acid inputs (NEFA uptake, DNL and three
FA per TG taken up from plasma) equal its outputs (beta-oxidation and three FA
per TG exported as VLDL). The check below works directly from the
`ini()` values.

```{r mass-balance}
p <- exp(unlist(mod$theta[grepl("^l", names(mod$theta))]))
names(p) <- sub("^l", "", names(p))
vldl <- p[["emax_vldl_prod"]] * p[["tg_er_basal"]] / (p[["ec50_vldl_prod"]] + p[["tg_er_basal"]])
fa_in <- p[["nefa_uptake_flux"]] + p[["dnl_basal_flux"]] +
  3 * p[["kuptake_liver_tg"]] * p[["tg_p_basal"]] * p[["vd_tg_p"]]
fa_out <- p[["kbetaox"]] * p[["fa_cy_basal"]] * p[["vd_cyt"]] + 3 * vldl
c(fa_in_mmol_day = fa_in, fa_out_mmol_day = fa_out, vldl_tg_mmol_day = vldl)
stopifnot(abs(fa_in / fa_out - 1) < 1e-8)
```

# Virtual population (Figure 2)

The authors drew 500,000 plausible patients with a Metropolis-Hastings
independence sampler and kept 1,900 virtual patients by acceptance-rejection.
That run is not reproducible here: the file of plausible patients in the code
deposit is a Git LFS pointer, not the data. The vignette therefore rebuilds a
smaller population with the same ingredients:

1. Draw the 14 searched parameters from the authors' prior. Each is log-normal
   with mean equal to its basal value and linear-scale SD `(HV - LV) / 3.24`
   (`mh.jl`).
2. Solve each draw to steady state. Discard any draw with a steady-state
   concentration outside the bounds in rows 23 to 27 of
   `parameters_pluto.csv` (`mh_sim.jl`).
3. Accept each plausible patient with probability proportional to
   `pdf(target) / local density of plausible patients`. The density comes from
   the median distance to the 5 nearest neighbours in (liver fat %, TG mM)
   space (`select_vps.jl`).

In step 1 the authors' Metropolis-Hastings chain targets prior x target pdf,
and their selection step then divides by the local density of those samples.
Drawing straight from the prior and dividing by the prior's density in
observable space reaches the same end point: the virtual patients' observables
follow the target distribution.

```{r vpop-tables}
# parameters_pluto.csv rows 1-14 (searched) and 23-27 (steady-state bounds)
prior_tab <- tibble::tribble(
  ~parameter, ~TV, ~LV, ~HV,
  "klipase_clear", 16.801971423166567, 2.6608094803554985, 66.52023700888748,
  "sens_nefa_uptake", 0.001, 1e-06, 0.1,
  "sens_betaox_dnl", 0.1, 0.010000000000000002, 0.2,
  "kuptake_er", 929.808692197991, 232.45217304949776, 3719.234768791964,
  "kuptake_liver_tg", 0.5734207183549842, 0.14335517958874605, 2.293682873419937,
  "ksynth_cy_tg", 14463.690767524306, 3615.9226918810764, 57854.76307009722,
  "klipo_cy_tg", 0.27914923181321905, 0.06978730795330476, 1.1165969272528762,
  "ksynth_er_tg", 129140.09613860988, 32285.02403465247, 516560.3845544395,
  "kbetaox", 1667.225980228621, 416.80649505715525, 6668.903920914484,
  "emax_vldl_prod", 33.62629534, 8.406573835, 134.50518136,
  "ec50_vldl_prod", 26.67240932642487, 6.668102331606217, 106.68963730569948,
  "chylo_basal_flux", 97.62521588946458, 46.37197754749568, 168.9264896373057,
  "dnl_basal_flux", 9.665448866236932, 0.9665448866236933, 77.32359092989546,
  "nefa_uptake_flux", 171.69402414356475, 85.84701207178237, 686.776096574259
)
state_bounds <- tibble::tribble(
  ~state, ~LV, ~HV,
  "fa_cy", 0.0375, 5.9192307692307695,
  "tg_cy", 3.332536469512164, 2300.2192108409736,
  "fa_er", 0.0375, 5.9192307692307695,
  "tg_er", 3.332536469512164, 2300.2192108409736,
  "tg_p", 0.38860103626943004, 9.715025906735752
)

# Joint log-normal of (liver fat %, 24-h mean TG mM): mean and covariance of
# log() of the 176 digitised Kotronen 2007 points in util.jl, TG divided by 0.8.
target_mu <- c(1.51335179, 0.4790895)
target_cov <- matrix(c(1.60254749, 0.26781155, 0.26781155, 0.30396876), 2)
```

```{r vpop-draw}
set.seed(20220719)
n_pp <- 20000
sd_lin <- (prior_tab$HV - prior_tab$LV) / 3.24
mu_log <- log(prior_tab$TV^2 / sqrt(sd_lin^2 + prior_tab$TV^2))
sd_log <- sqrt(log(1 + sd_lin^2 / prior_tab$TV^2))
draws <- vapply(
  seq_len(nrow(prior_tab)),
  function(i) exp(rnorm(n_pp, mu_log[i], sd_log[i])),
  numeric(n_pp)
)
colnames(draws) <- prior_tab$parameter

# Map onto ini() names: everything except the two feedback exponents is
# log-transformed.
log_par <- setdiff(prior_tab$parameter, c("sens_nefa_uptake", "sens_betaox_dnl"))
pp_par <- as.data.frame(draws)
pp_par[log_par] <- log(pp_par[log_par])
names(pp_par)[match(log_par, names(pp_par))] <- paste0("l", log_par)
pp_par$id <- seq_len(n_pp)

# 10,000 days is the end of the authors' steady-state search window.
pp_ss <- rxSolve(
  mod,
  params = pp_par,
  events = data.frame(id = pp_par$id, time = 10000, evid = 0),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

```{r vpop-select}
in_bounds <- Reduce(`&`, lapply(seq_len(nrow(state_bounds)), function(i) {
  x <- pp_ss[[state_bounds$state[i]]]
  !is.na(x) & x >= state_bounds$LV[i] & x <= state_bounds$HV[i]
}))
pp <- pp_ss[in_bounds, ]

dlnorm2 <- function(lf, tg, mu, sigma) {
  z <- cbind(log(lf) - mu[1], log(tg) - mu[2])
  q <- rowSums((z %*% solve(sigma)) * z)
  exp(-q / 2) / (2 * pi * sqrt(det(sigma)) * lf * tg)
}
knn_median_dist <- function(x, k = 5) {
  # Median of the k nearest distances, the point itself included (select_vps.jl).
  vapply(seq_len(nrow(x)), function(i) {
    d <- sqrt((x[, 1] - x[i, 1])^2 + (x[, 2] - x[i, 2])^2)
    stats::median(sort.int(d, partial = seq_len(k))[seq_len(k)])
  }, numeric(1))
}

obs <- cbind(pp$liver_fat, pp$tg_p)
pdf_target <- dlnorm2(pp$liver_fat, pp$tg_p, target_mu, target_cov)
rho <- 5 / (pi * knn_median_dist(obs)^2)
p_incl <- pdf_target / rho
selected <- runif(nrow(pp)) < p_incl / max(p_incl)
vp <- pp[selected, ]
vp$nafld <- vp$liver_fat > 5

c(
  plausible_in_bounds = nrow(pp),
  virtual_patients = nrow(vp),
  nafld = sum(vp$nafld)
)
```

Of the virtual patients, `r round(100 * mean(vp$nafld))`% have liver fat above
5%. The paper had 900 of 1,900 (47%), and the target distribution implies 47%.
The table compares the log-scale moments of the rebuilt population with the
target.

```{r vpop-moments}
vp_moments <- tibble::tibble(
  Statistic = c("mean log liver fat", "SD log liver fat", "mean log TG", "SD log TG", "correlation"),
  Target = c(target_mu[1], sqrt(target_cov[1, 1]), target_mu[2], sqrt(target_cov[2, 2]),
             target_cov[1, 2] / sqrt(target_cov[1, 1] * target_cov[2, 2])),
  `Virtual population` = c(
    mean(log(vp$liver_fat)), sd(log(vp$liver_fat)),
    mean(log(vp$tg_p)), sd(log(vp$tg_p)),
    cor(log(vp$liver_fat), log(vp$tg_p))
  )
)
knitr::kable(vp_moments, digits = 3)

stopifnot(
  abs(mean(log(vp$liver_fat)) - target_mu[1]) < 0.3,
  abs(mean(log(vp$tg_p)) - target_mu[2]) < 0.15,
  abs(mean(vp$nafld) - 0.47) < 0.1
)
```

```{r fig2, fig.height = 5}
theta <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 200)
ev <- eigen(target_cov)
ellipse <- t(target_mu + ev$vectors %*% (sqrt(ev$values * qchisq(0.95, 2)) * rbind(cos(theta), sin(theta))))
ggplot(vp, aes(log(liver_fat), log(tg_p), colour = nafld)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
  geom_path(
    data = data.frame(x = ellipse[, 1], y = ellipse[, 2]),
    aes(x, y), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "steelblue", `TRUE` = "firebrick"),
                      labels = c("liver fat <= 5%", "NAFLD (> 5%)"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "log(liver fat, %)", y = "log(24-h mean plasma TG, mM)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Rieger 2022. Ellipse: 95% region of the target distribution.") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Pioglitazone and diet (Figures 3 and 4)

The paper validates the model on two interventions, both simulated in the
NAFLD virtual patients with no refitting:

* **Pioglitazone 45 mg QD for 24 weeks** (Belfort 2006): NEFA release from
  adipose falls by 27.5% (`scale_nefa_uptake = 0.725`).
* **Diet for 26 weeks** (Haufe 2013): chylomicron input -20%, DNL -55.2%, NEFA
  flux -11% (`scale_chylo = 0.8`, `scale_dnl = 0.448`,
  `scale_nefa_uptake = 0.89`).

Each virtual patient runs to its steady state over 10,000 days at
`scale_* = 1`. The multipliers then step to their treatment values as
time-varying data columns, which override the `ini()` values from that row
onward. At most 200 NAFLD virtual patients are used in each arm.

```{r intervention-helper}
nafld_vp <- vp |>
  filter(nafld) |>
  slice_head(n = 200) |>
  select(id)
nafld_par <- pp_par[match(nafld_vp$id, pp_par$id), ]
nafld_par$id <- seq_len(nrow(nafld_par))

t_run_in <- 10000
run_intervention <- function(scales, weeks, par = nafld_par) {
  ev <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = par$id, time = c(0, t_run_in, t_run_in + 7 * weeks))
  ev$evid <- 0
  for (nm in c("scale_chylo", "scale_dnl", "scale_nefa_uptake", "scale_tg_ester", "scale_vldl_prod")) {
    value <- if (nm %in% names(scales)) scales[[nm]] else 1
    ev[[nm]] <- ifelse(ev$time >= t_run_in, value, 1)
  }
  sim <- rxSolve(mod, params = par, events = ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  # rxSolve() drops the id column for a single subject.
  if (!"id" %in% names(sim)) sim$id <- 1L
  sim |>
    filter(time >= t_run_in) |>
    mutate(phase = ifelse(time == t_run_in, "baseline", "end")) |>
    select(id, phase, liver_fat, tg_cy, tg_er) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = phase, values_from = c(liver_fat, tg_cy, tg_er)) |>
    mutate(pct_change = 100 * (liver_fat_end / liver_fat_baseline - 1))
}

pio <- run_intervention(c(scale_nefa_uptake = 0.725), weeks = 24)
diet <- run_intervention(c(scale_chylo = 0.8, scale_dnl = 0.448, scale_nefa_uptake = 0.89), weeks = 26)
```

In `main.jl`, the code that produced Figures 3 to 5 computes baseline liver
fat with `getLTGprct`'s vector method, which uses a non-TG hepatocyte volume of
0.95 x 0.7089 = 0.673 L. It computes the end-of-treatment value with the
matrix method, which uses `vd_cyt + vd_er` = 0.655 L. The packaged
`liver_fat` output uses 0.673 L at both time points. The "as coded" column
recomputes the end value the way the figure code does, to show how far the
mismatch moves the published means.

```{r fig34-table}
as_coded_end <- function(d, vd_cyt = 0.4962299999999999, vd_er = 0.15879359999999998) {
  v <- (d$tg_cy_end * vd_cyt + d$tg_er_end * vd_er) * 772 / 1000 / 900
  100 * v / (v + vd_cyt + vd_er)
}
summarise_arm <- function(d) {
  coded <- 100 * (as_coded_end(d) / d$liver_fat_baseline - 1)
  c(mean = mean(d$pct_change), sd = stats::sd(d$pct_change), mean_as_coded = mean(coded))
}
fig34 <- tibble::tibble(
  Intervention = c("Pioglitazone, 24 weeks", "Diet, 26 weeks"),
  `Observed mean (SD)` = c("-54 (5.4)", "-44.6 (19.3)"),
  `Published simulation mean (SD)` = c("-50.4 (12.0)", "-43.5 (13.0)"),
  `This vignette, mean` = c(summarise_arm(pio)[["mean"]], summarise_arm(diet)[["mean"]]),
  `This vignette, SD` = c(summarise_arm(pio)[["sd"]], summarise_arm(diet)[["sd"]]),
  `This vignette, mean as coded` = c(summarise_arm(pio)[["mean_as_coded"]], summarise_arm(diet)[["mean_as_coded"]])
)
knitr::kable(fig34, digits = 1)

stopifnot(
  abs(mean(pio$pct_change) - (-50.4)) < 8,
  abs(mean(diet$pct_change) - (-43.5)) < 8
)
```

The observed values are Belfort 2006 and Haufe 2013 as given in `main.jl`
(`data_pio_mean`, `data_diet_mean` and their SDs). The published simulation
means and SDs were digitised by the maintainers from the error bars in Figures 3
and 4. Digitising the observed bars in the same figures returns -54.0 (5.4) and
-44.6 (19.3), which confirms the digitisation.

```{r fig34, fig.height = 3.8}
bind_rows(
  mutate(pio, Intervention = "Pioglitazone (Figure 3)"),
  mutate(diet, Intervention = "Diet (Figure 4)")
) |>
  ggplot(aes(Intervention, pct_change)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "darkorange", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(
    data = data.frame(
      Intervention = c("Pioglitazone (Figure 3)", "Diet (Figure 4)"),
      pct_change = c(-54, -44.6)
    ),
    colour = "purple", size = 3
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = data.frame(
      Intervention = c("Pioglitazone (Figure 3)", "Diet (Figure 4)"),
      pct_change = c(-50.4, -43.5)
    ),
    colour = "black", shape = 4, size = 3
  ) +
  labs(
    y = "Change in liver fat (%)", x = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figures 3, 4 and S1 of Rieger 2022. Violins: NAFLD virtual patients;",
      "purple: observed mean; cross: published simulated mean."
    )
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-100, 0)) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Sensitivity analysis (Figure 5)

Each of four fluxes is held at a constant inhibition for 26 weeks: DNL, NEFA
uptake and cytosolic esterification are scaled by `1 - inhibition`. VLDL
export is instead activated by `1 / (1 - inhibition)`, so 95% on the x-axis
means 20-fold activation. The curves are means over the NAFLD virtual patients.

```{r fig5}
inhibition <- c(0, 10, 25, 50, 75, 90, 95)
sa_targets <- c(DNL = "scale_dnl", `NEFA uptake` = "scale_nefa_uptake",
                Esterification = "scale_tg_ester", `VLDL synthesis (activated)` = "scale_vldl_prod")
sa <- bind_rows(lapply(names(sa_targets), function(lbl) {
  bind_rows(lapply(inhibition, function(inh) {
    value <- if (lbl == "VLDL synthesis (activated)") 1 / (1 - inh / 100) else 1 - inh / 100
    d <- run_intervention(stats::setNames(value, sa_targets[[lbl]]), weeks = 26)
    tibble::tibble(
      intervention = lbl, inhibition = inh,
      mean_pct_change = mean(d$pct_change),
      mean_as_coded = mean(100 * (as_coded_end(d) / d$liver_fat_baseline - 1))
    )
  }))
}))

ggplot(sa, aes(inhibition, mean_pct_change, colour = intervention)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-100, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Mean inhibition (%)", y = "Change in liver fat (%)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Rieger 2022 (NAFLD virtual-patient mean).") +
  theme_bw()
```

The maintainers digitised the Figure 5 curves at 25, 50, 75 and 90% inhibition
(colour-matched pixel columns). The published curves were computed with the
mismatched end-of-treatment hepatocyte volume described above. For small
changes the mismatch is most visible: it makes the VLDL curve about 2.5 points
less negative. So the comparison is made on the "as coded" column.

```{r fig5-table}
fig5_pub <- tibble::tribble(
  ~intervention, ~inhibition, ~published,
  "DNL", 25, -8.2, "DNL", 50, -18.4, "DNL", 75, -30.7, "DNL", 90, -41.9,
  "NEFA uptake", 25, -46.8, "NEFA uptake", 50, -75.9, "NEFA uptake", 75, -91.1, "NEFA uptake", 90, -95.4,
  "Esterification", 25, -16.3, "Esterification", 50, -36.5, "Esterification", 75, -58.7, "Esterification", 90, -72.7,
  "VLDL synthesis (activated)", 25, -7.8, "VLDL synthesis (activated)", 50, -10.2,
  "VLDL synthesis (activated)", 75, -11.6, "VLDL synthesis (activated)", 90, -12.2
)
fig5_cmp <- inner_join(fig5_pub, sa, by = c("intervention", "inhibition")) |>
  mutate(difference = mean_as_coded - published)
fig5_cmp |>
  rename(
    Intervention = intervention, `Inhibition (%)` = inhibition,
    `Published (digitised)` = published, `This vignette` = mean_pct_change,
    `This vignette, as coded` = mean_as_coded, `Difference, as coded` = difference
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

# The ranking the paper reports (NEFA uptake > esterification > DNL > VLDL) at
# 90% inhibition, and agreement with the digitised curves. The bounds are on the
# centre and a robust quantile because the virtual population is a random draw.
rank_at <- function(inh) {
  x <- sa[sa$inhibition == inh, ]
  x$intervention[order(x$mean_pct_change)]
}
stopifnot(
  identical(rank_at(90), c("NEFA uptake", "Esterification", "DNL", "VLDL synthesis (activated)")),
  abs(median(fig5_cmp$difference)) < 3,
  quantile(abs(fig5_cmp$difference), 0.9) < 5
)
```

# Typical patient

For reference, the same interventions applied to the typical (basal)
parameter set give the following responses. The typical patient sits just
below the NAFLD threshold.

```{r typical}
typ_par <- data.frame(id = 1)
typ <- bind_rows(
  run_intervention(c(scale_nefa_uptake = 0.725), 24, typ_par) |> mutate(Intervention = "Pioglitazone, 24 weeks"),
  run_intervention(c(scale_chylo = 0.8, scale_dnl = 0.448, scale_nefa_uptake = 0.89), 26, typ_par) |>
    mutate(Intervention = "Diet, 26 weeks")
)
typ |>
  select(Intervention, liver_fat_baseline, liver_fat_end, pct_change) |>
  rename(
    `Baseline liver fat (%)` = liver_fat_baseline, `End liver fat (%)` = liver_fat_end,
    `Change (%)` = pct_change
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Source of the equations.** The article prints no equations. The model is
  transcribed from the authors' Zenodo code deposit (v1.1,
  doi:10.5281/zenodo.6621096), which the article cites as the full
  specification. Every value matches Supplementary Table S1 to the two
  significant figures printed there.
* **Pioglitazone effect size.** Section 2.5 reports a -28% change in NEFA
  uptake. The code uses `1 - 0.275`, and that value is packaged as the
  intervention setting. Section 3.2 attributes the NEFA reduction to "the
  Haufe et al. (2013) study"; the Methods and the code make clear it comes from
  Belfort 2006.
* **Diet DNL reduction.** Section 2.6 reports -55%; the code uses
  `scale_dnl = 0.448` (-55.2%), which is used here.
* **Liver-fat observable.** The figure code uses two different non-TG
  hepatocyte volumes, 0.673 L at baseline and 0.655 L at the end of treatment.
  The packaged `liver_fat` output uses 0.673 L throughout, the value the
  authors used to select virtual patients (`mh_sim.jl`, `GetObs`). The "as
  coded" column above shows the effect of the mismatch on the published means.
* **Virtual population.** The authors' 500,000 plausible patients are not in
  the deposit (`save_pp.jld2` is a Git LFS pointer). The vignette rebuilds a
  smaller population from 20,000 prior draws by direct acceptance-rejection
  rather than a Metropolis-Hastings chain. The selection weights and the target
  distribution follow the source code, so the rebuilt population matches the
  target moments but is not the published one.
* **Interventions as data columns.** The authors change the parameter vector
  and restart the ODE from each patient's steady state. Here the `scale_*`
  multipliers are passed as time-varying columns in the event table after a
  10,000-day run-in, which is equivalent.
* **No IIV or residual error.** Variability lives entirely in the virtual
  population. The packaged model is the deterministic basal patient, and its
  `ini()` values are all fixed.
